\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{كهرباء} (kahrabāʾ)}{كهرباء (kahrabāʾ)}]{\ar{كهرباء} (kahrabāʾ) — electricity}

\label{lesson:AR-C444-kahraba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to overlook, then the Arabic for a strongbox.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{كهرباء}}
\textbf{\ar{كهرباء}} — \emph{kahrabāʾ} — \textquotedblleft{}electricity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تعمل} \ar{الثلاجة} \ar{بالكهرباء}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taʿmalu ath-thallāja bi-l-kahrabāʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The fridge runs on electricity.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{كهرباء}} (\emph{kahrabāʾ}) goes back to Persian \emph{kahrubā}, \textquotedblleft{}amber\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), a name usually read as \textquotedblleft{}straw-robber\textquotedblright{}, since rubbed amber draws straw to it; the old name passed to electricity.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kahrabāʾ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kahrabāʾ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿmalu ath-thallāja bi-l-kahrabāʾ.} — The fridge runs on electricity.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to overlook, then the Arabic for a strongbox, then say \emph{kahrabāʾ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{كهرباء} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Electricity\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{سخن} (sakhkhana)}{سخن (sakhkhana)}]{\ar{سخن} (sakhkhana) — to heat up}

\label{lesson:AR-C444-sakhkhana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a strongbox, then the Arabic for electricity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{سخن}}
\textbf{\ar{سخن}} — \emph{sakhkhana} — \textquotedblleft{}to heat up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سخنت} \ar{أمي} \ar{الحساء}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sakhkhanat ummī al-ḥasāʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother heated up the soup.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يسخن}, \emph{yusakhkhin}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{سخن}} (\emph{sakhkhana}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-kh-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to be hot\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, \textquotedblleft{}to make hot\textquotedblright{}, beside \emph{sākhin}, \textquotedblleft{}hot\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sakhkhana}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sakhkhanat ummī al-ḥasāʾ.} — My mother heated up the soup.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a strongbox, then the Arabic for electricity, then say \emph{sakhkhana} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انقطع} (inqaṭaʿa)}{انقطع (inqaṭaʿa)}]{\ar{انقطع} (inqaṭaʿa) — to be cut off}

\label{lesson:AR-C444-inqataa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for electricity, then the Arabic for to heat up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انقطع}}
\textbf{\ar{انقطع}} — \emph{inqaṭaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to be cut off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انقطعت} \ar{الكهرباء} \ar{في} \ar{الفندق} \ar{ليلة} \ar{أمس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{inqaṭaʿat al-kahrabāʾ fī al-funduq laylat ams.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The electricity was cut off in the hotel last night.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينقطع}, \emph{yanqaṭiʿ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انقطع}} (\emph{inqaṭaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-ṭ-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to cut\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VII, \textquotedblleft{}to be cut\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{محول} (muḥawwil)}{محول (muḥawwil)}]{\ar{محول} (muḥawwil) — an adapter; a transformer}

\label{lesson:AR-C444-muhawwil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to heat up, then the Arabic for to be cut off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{محول}}
\textbf{\ar{محول}} — \emph{muḥawwil} — \textquotedblleft{}an adapter; a transformer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{احتجت} \ar{إلى} \ar{محول} \ar{لشاحن} \ar{الهاتف}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iḥtajtu ilā muḥawwil li-shāḥin al-hātif.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I needed an adapter for the phone charger.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{محول}} (\emph{muḥawwil}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-w-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to change, to shift\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the Form II participle, \textquotedblleft{}a thing that converts\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muḥawwil}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to heat up, then the Arabic for to be cut off, then say \emph{muḥawwil} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أنار} (anāra)}{أنار (anāra)}]{\ar{أنار} (anāra) — to light up}

\label{lesson:AR-C444-anara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to be cut off, then the Arabic for an adapter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أنار}}
\textbf{\ar{أنار}} — \emph{anāra} — \textquotedblleft{}to light up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أنار} \ar{المصباح} \ar{الممر} \ar{الطويل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{anāra al-miṣbāḥ al-mamarr aṭ-ṭawīl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The lamp lit up the long corridor.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينير}, \emph{yunīr}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أنار}} (\emph{anāra}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-w-r}, \textquotedblleft{}light\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV, \textquotedblleft{}to give light\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}
